title: CatchUp AI Engineering & WebRTC Architecture Sync

summary.executive: The engineering team evaluated the real-time recording and automated post-meeting AI pipeline for CatchUp AI. Alex presented the client-side MediaRecorder pipeline coupled with server-side WebSocket signaling. The team verified that multi-track audio mixing ensures crystal clear transcripts even with simultaneous crosstalk. Target latency for AI summary generation is set under 15 seconds after call termination.
keyDecisions: Adopt dual-mode recording: client-side composite stream capture + server-side audio backup.
Use Web Speech API for zero-latency live captions during the live call, and enhance with deep LLM post-processing.
Store video recordings in IndexedDB locally with cloud synchronization capability.
Set maximum auto-summary generation target to under 15 seconds post call.
topicsDiscussed: WebRTC peer mesh vs SFU fallback under high concurrency
MediaRecorder codec compatibility across Chromium and Safari
Structured JSON schema extraction for AI action items
Interactive timeline scrubbing with chapter bounding boxes

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: Good afternoon everyone! Let's get right into our engineering sync. The primary agenda today is CatchUp AI's recording pipeline and post-meeting intelligence.

transcript.speaker: Alex Rivera
transcript.text: Thanks Sarah. We've finalized the client-side MediaRecorder pipeline. As soon as any meeting starts, it seamlessly records both the composite canvas and multi-track audio.

transcript.speaker: Priya Sharma
transcript.text: From a user perspective, this completely removes the pain of remembering to hit record or having a bot intrude awkwardly into the room.

transcript.speaker: Alex Rivera
transcript.text: Exactly. And for missed meetings, anyone with the link can scrub through chapters, click any line in the transcript to jump to that moment in the video, or simply read the TL;DR.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Vance
transcript.text: Regarding server load: the WebSocket signaling handles peer coordination, while the heavy video rendering is handled smoothly on modern browsers via Canvas and WebCodecs.

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: The action items extraction looks incredible. Can we ensure each action item has a clear assignee and priority tag?

transcript.speaker: Alex Rivera
transcript.text: Yes, our prompt schema extracts the task, speaker context, designated owner, and target deadline into clean structured JSON.

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: Awesome. Let's make sure the interactive Q&A assistant is prominently placed so anyone can query the meeting directly.

transcript.speaker: Alex Rivera
transcript.text: Done. CatchUp Copilot is ready. Let's wrap up and get this deployed for testing.
